operations.value:
internal/cli's tests now build configuration-ledger commits by hand in three separate places, each reproducing what gitstore's writeConfigObjects does — the two blobs, one tree and one commit every configuration commit is made of.

- writeFutureConfigCommit in newerwriter_test.go, forging a project written by a build AHEAD of this one.
- writeLegacyPriorityLessLedger in priority_log_test.go, forging a genesis from a build BEHIND this one, with no priorities section.
- legacyDisplayConfiguredRepository in priority_color_test.go, forging the same era but display-configured and still at the older reader generation.

Each is justified. There is no other way to test a project this build cannot itself produce, and two of the three were written independently, days apart, by people solving different problems. That is the point: nobody chose to have three.

## Why it is worth doing

They share the delicate half — encoding a pack, applying it, writing the objects, pointing the ref — and differ only in what configuration goes in. When the configuration commit's shape changes, all three need the same edit, and whichever one the author does not happen to be looking at will be missed. It will fail as a confusing test error in an unrelated package rather than as anything that names the cause.

## What to do

Extract the shared construction into one test helper that takes the configuration to record, and express all three call sites through it. The differences that must survive are the reader generation stamped on the document, whether a priorities section is present, and the display settings — everything else is the same four objects.

Keep each call site's comment explaining WHY that particular shape is unreachable through the ordinary write path. Those comments are the valuable part and they are all different; only the plumbing is duplicated.

## Not urgent

Nothing is broken. All three work and are covered by passing tests. This is about the edit that has not happened yet.
